\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لعنت} (lānat)}{لعنت (lānat)}]{\ur{لعنت} (lānat) — a curse}

\label{lesson:UR-C326-lanat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a ghost, then the Urdu for a witch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لعنت}}
\textbf{\ur{لعنت}} — \emph{lānat} — \textquotedblleft{}a curse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سب} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{پر} \ur{لعنت} \ur{بھیجی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sab ne us par lānat bhejī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone cursed him.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لعنت}} (\emph{lānat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{laʿna}, \textquotedblleft{}a curse\textquotedblright{}. A curse is sent: \textbf{\ur{لعنت} \ur{بھیجی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lānat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lānat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sab ne us par lānat bhejī.} — Everyone cursed him.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a ghost, then the Urdu for a witch, then say \emph{lānat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{لعنت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A curse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کوسنا} (kosnā)}{کوسنا (kosnā)}]{\ur{کوسنا} (kosnā) — to curse; to rail at}

\label{lesson:UR-C326-kosna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a witch, then the Urdu for a curse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کوسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کوسنا}} — \emph{kosnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to curse; to rail at\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادی} \ur{نے} \ur{بادشاہ} \ur{کو} \ur{کوسا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī ne bādshāh ko kosā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother cursed the king.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{اسے} \ur{کوسا}, \emph{us ne use kosā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کوسنا}} (\emph{kosnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{kosnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to curse\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{kr\'{\={o}}śati}, \textquotedblleft{}cries out\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3612).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kosnā}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پچھتانا} (pachhtānā)}{پچھتانا (pachhtānā)}]{\ur{پچھتانا} (pachhtānā) — to regret; to repent}

\label{lesson:UR-C326-pachhtana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a curse, then the Urdu for to rail at.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پچھتانا}}
\textbf{\ur{پچھتانا}} — \emph{pachhtānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to regret; to repent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بعد} \ur{میں} \ur{بادشاہ} \ur{پچھتایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bād meṅ bādshāh pachhtāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Later the king regretted it.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پچھتایا}, \emph{voh pachhtāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پچھتانا}} (\emph{pachhtānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pachtānā} under \emph{*paścōttāpa}, a burning afterwards, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 8010): the pain that comes after the deed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{روٹھنا} (rūṭhnā)}{روٹھنا (rūṭhnā)}]{\ur{روٹھنا} (rūṭhnā) — to sulk; to take offence}

\label{lesson:UR-C326-ruthna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to rail at, then the Urdu for to regret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{روٹھنا}}
\textbf{\ur{روٹھنا}} — \emph{rūṭhnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to sulk; to take offence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بہن} \ur{ہم} \ur{سے} \ur{روٹھ} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bahan ham se rūṭh gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister went off in a sulk with us.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{روٹھ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh rūṭh gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{روٹھنا}} (\emph{rūṭhnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{rūṭhnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be offended\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{ruṣṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}angry\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10791). The person you sulk with takes \textbf{\ur{سے}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عذاب} (azāb)}{عذاب (azāb)}]{\ur{عذاب} (azāb) — torment; a punishing suffering}

\label{lesson:UR-C326-azab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to regret, then the Urdu for to sulk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عذاب}}
\textbf{\ur{عذاب}} — \emph{azāb} — \textquotedblleft{}torment; a punishing suffering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{قحط} \ur{ایک} \ur{عذاب} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih qahat ek azāb thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This famine was a torment.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عذاب}} (\emph{azāb}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿadhāb}, \textquotedblleft{}torment, punishment\textquotedblright{}. Urdu says its middle letter as \emph{z}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{azāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{azāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih qahat ek azāb thā.} — This famine was a torment.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to regret, then the Urdu for to sulk, then say \emph{azāb} again
\end{itemize}
